differences.what: T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.

T-2564: the pinnacle caps are ogival with a moulded collar and ball finial, the rear one seated on the coping, and the rounded coping sweeps up into the corner pinnacle on the return and at both front corners.
Most of Keith is occluded by Glessner or outside this frame. Its bow, stair, lower ornament and rear cannot be accepted from this view. The isolated render does not include the occluding neighbour.

T-2579: the camera is re-fitted to six controls (both return pinnacle apexes; the northernmost third-storey light's head, sill and south jamb; the lattice coping's north end): RMS 4.0 px, about 0.09 m at 60 m. The pinnacles, lattice, upper lights and the north return now register; the return depth agrees with the model.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.

T-2578 ruling: the stone parapet stops at the rear pinnacle. Every picture that sees that corner (1887, Taylor 2135, the 1888 Glessner plate, the c. 1888 view looking SW, the Glessner front, 1948) shows sky straight behind it, or in 1948 a darker wall about a course lower; the model drops it there.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.
T-2578: the 1887-89 cowl ventilator is gone by 1948 (a low dark stub stands at its foot, just inside the rear pinnacle); the 1886 phase keeps it.

T-2579: under the lattice the photographs show a narrow fillet and then a band of small, staggered, diamond-pointed units about 1 m deep directly below the openings; the model puts a deeper plain band and a moulding there and lays larger rock-faced blocks in five courses lower down, so its band reads taller and lower than the pictures'. T-2679: built as these pictures show it: five staggered rows of diamond-pointed units (a point on each, in the front's rock-faced stone, on a dressed ground in a checker), 0.84 m deep with its top at the foot of the moulded course under the lattice, the street cornice box above that course brought back to a 0.06 m fillet, and plain ground 0.28 m down to the head band.

T-2579: a carved boss stands on the north-east corner pier at the foot of the lattice, in this view and the Glessner-front view; the model has none. T-2679: built: a lobed boss about 0.34 m across on the north-east corner, ending the moulded course under the lattice, which now stops 0.34 m short of the corner.

T-2679: the units read bulkier here, filling more of each row with less ground between the points; their section is below the picture's grain and is drawn, not read. T-2714: the band's units repeat every 10 px along a row in the photograph and 11 px in this render (about 13 px before, at 0.336 m), so the points now stand as close as the photograph's with the ground between them halved; the rows and their depth were already in register. What still differs is the unit's section, rounded lumps here against cut points, which is below this picture's grain and is drawn (L-k01-keith-boss-2679).

T-2680: the lattice and coping stood high over the moulded course. With the third-storey light in register, the lower row read at 15.48-15.74 m against the photograph's 15.25-15.53 m and the upper row 0.2 m high likewise, with the moulded course standing as a deep stack between the lattice and the boss. The crown is now 0.2 m lower, and the course stays level with the boss as it is here. The rows read within 3-5 px (about 0.1 m, near this camera's 2.7 px RMS), and the coping, band and head band within a few pixels.

T-2813: re-rendered with Keith's crown 0.16 m lower (the moulded course under the lattice 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, the checker and head bands unmoved); its camera re-solved on the moved crown controls (2.73 to 3.20 px RMS, tools/keith_crown_resolve.py). Read again at the crown beside the previous render: the lattice, coping and pinnacles move a few pixels at this picture's scale and nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands as it was (matches).

T-2876: re-rendered on the GLB in the tree, T-2845's loggia (0.6 m pedestals at the first-floor plan's place, each pair's shafts 0.36 m apart, the flight 1.8 m clear and the stoop 0.15 m south), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia and flight (x 12-361, y 250-942). Here the loggia is mostly hidden: a dark lattice stands over its south end and 1812's ivy wall over its north end, and the camera is fitted on the crown and upper lights only (six controls 10-17 m up, the eye height held), so the one pair it shows, about 30 px left of the render's north pair, is that fit's extrapolation to the ground, not a reading of the loggia's place, which the plate rules. It stays under this record's not-shown item for the lower front. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict returns to matches.

T-2881: re-rendered on the loggia with its rear row built (a pedestal 0.6 m square against the wall behind each front one, carrying a pair of turned shafts 0.39 m off the wall at a 0.28 m pitch, their radii 0.78 of the front's, under a paired capital; tools/keith_loggia_rear_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-rear-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 81-231, y 701-843); the loggia is mostly hidden here behind the dark lattice and 1812's ivy wall, and the camera is fitted on the crown (T-2876), so the rear north pair now drawn behind the north front pair is not read. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict returns to matches.

T-2882: re-rendered on the loggia with a respond on the wall behind each rear pair (a flat pier the rear pedestal's width, 0.25 m deep, from the pedestal's top to the ceiling; tools/keith_loggia_respond_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-respond-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 96-239, y 703-804); the rear row stands behind the respond's face, and this picture does not read the rear row, for the reason T-2881's item above gives, so it does not read the respond either. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands (matches).

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
